newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Asia Fuel Oil - Fuel oil supported, LSWR firm.
newsitem.headline: Asia Fuel Oil - Fuel oil supported, LSWR firm.

text.p: The Singapore high sulphur fuel oil prices were well supported with increased bids and offers on Wednesday, traders said.
Interest was seen in both the 180-cst and the 380-cst grade, they said.
After several 180-cst grade cargoes were traded since last week, offers were heard as high as $102.50 per tonne on Wednesday for lifting in the first half of July but bids were scarce.
The 180-cst grade was traded at $101.50 on Monday.
Bids for the 380-cst grade were heard at $95.75 per tonne for late July delivery, traders said.
The market is closely watching movement by a Singapore-based trader, who said the company was seeking to cover its short positions, and its sister company.
The two companies have bought four cargoes since last week.
"It seems the two companies are switching some of its interest in the gas oil market to fuel oil," said one trader.

Some traders said the Singapore trader was buying the cargoes to supply Indonesia, whose state oil firm Pertamina is expected to shut down some units in the 200,000-barrel-per-day (bpd) Balikpapan refinery for maintenance from July 10 for 32 days.

Despite the upward momentum, some traders said China may import more high sulphur fuel oil from South Korea with Seoul's imminent cut on domestic sulphur content to 0.5 percent from one percent in July, traders said
"South Korea may take away even more high sulphur fuel oil business from Singapore," said one trader. "But it has been taking away business from Singapore anyway."

In the low sulphur waxy residue (LSWR) market, traders said sentiment was firm on talk that Indonesia's Pertamina would decrease its July allocation to as low as 2.3 million barrels because of the refinery shutdown.
Pertamina has yet to announce its July allocation details. It allocated 3.1 million barrels in June, with additional 500,000 barrels rolled over from May.
Some one million barrels of Indonesian LSWR have been shipped to Japan so far this month, with demand expected to rise in July as Japan moves into summer, traders said.
South Korean, Australia and Italy will maintain their usual LSWR demand, tightening the supplies in July, traders noted.
"Demand increases but supplies decrease," said one trader. "Prices will just go up."
A Japanese trader said he saw prices at above 80 cents per barrel over the Pertamina formula.
A Singapore trader said bids were heard at $15.50 per barrel in the Singapore market but failed to attract sellers.
"Supplies are pretty tight now," he said, seeing prices to breach $16.00 per barrel soon.
